nri-world.title: Five Indian Americans Just Won Primaries Across Georgia. One Could Become the State's First South Asian Lieutenant Governor.

nri-world.title: The Diaspora Just Got Its Own Trade Portal. India's New York Consulate Built It.
nri-world.excerpt: At GLO-INDIA's inaugural Icons of Impact gala, Ambassador Binaya Pradhan unveiled a digital platform connecting Indian exporters with American buyers — a practical tool aimed at doubling bilateral trade to $500 billion by 2030.
nri-world.image_caption: Professionals deliberating at a diaspora networking event
nri-world.nri_angle: The India-USA Trade Facilitation Portal positions diaspora professionals as the connective tissue in bilateral commerce, offering MSMEs, women-led businesses, and ODOP artisans a bridge to American markets that previously required expensive intermediaries.

nri-world.title: A New Manhattan Restaurant Maps the Diaspora Through Its Menu. The Atlas Is Delicious.
nri-world.excerpt: Chef Aarthi Sampath's Drāvida traces South Asian flavours from Trinidad to Sri Lanka to Guyana — cuisines born in migration, now served in a restored East Village building with century-old brick ovens.
nri-world.image_caption: Hands preparing a South Asian dish with aromatic spices in a cooking pan
nri-world.nri_angle: Drāvida represents a new wave of diaspora dining that refuses to flatten South Asian food into a single 'Indian' category — it celebrates the culinary traditions born when Indians moved to the Caribbean, East Africa, Southeast Asia and beyond, giving second-generation diners a menu that mirrors their own layered identities.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: A Man Tore an Indian Flag Outside Frisco City Hall. The Community's Response Said More Than the Video.
nri-world.excerpt: An anti-immigration protest in a fast-growing North Texas suburb turned personal on June 3 when a protester ripped the Indian tricolour while anti-India slogans echoed behind him. For Frisco's Indian American families, the incident crystallised tensions they had been navigating quietly for months.
nri-world.image_caption: Indian Americans gathered at a community event celebrating cultural heritage
nri-world.nri_angle: The Frisco incident exposes the friction between rapid Indian American demographic growth in Sun Belt suburbs and a broader nativist backlash — forcing a community that has largely preferred quiet achievement to confront the limits of that strategy.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India's Trade Deal With Oman Just Went Live. For 700,000 Gulf Indians, It's More Than Tariffs.
nri-world.excerpt: The India-Oman CEPA, which entered into force on June 1, is Oman's first bilateral trade agreement since the US deal in 2006 — and it includes mobility provisions that could reshape how Indian professionals work in the Gulf.
nri-world.image_caption: Aerial view of Muscat port with ship, cranes, and mountains in the background
nri-world.nri_angle: Nearly 700,000 Indians live in Oman, many in merchant families with roots stretching back two centuries. The CEPA's enhanced mobility provisions — easing entry for accountants, architects, healthcare workers — directly affect the professional class of the Gulf diaspora.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Five South Asian Candidates Just Won Georgia Primaries. One Could Become the State's First Sikh Official.
nri-world.excerpt: In a state with 600,000 Asian American residents, Indian and South Asian candidates swept five races in the May 19 primary — including a milestone for the Sikh community that Georgia has never seen.
nri-world.image_caption: The Georgia State Capitol in Atlanta, where newly elected South Asian lawmakers will take their seats
nri-world.nri_angle: Indian and South Asian Americans are building political power in Georgia at an unprecedented pace — from state house seats to a potential lieutenant governorship. The results mark a generational shift in how the diaspora engages with American democracy beyond the coasts.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India's $135 Billion Remittance Lifeline Is Under Pressure From Three Directions at Once.
nri-world.excerpt: AI-driven tech layoffs, a $100,000 H-1B visa fee, and a new US remittance levy are squeezing the financial pipeline that covers nearly half of India's trade deficit — and the consequences are about to reach millions of NRI families.
nri-world.image_caption: A currency exchange office window displaying conversion rates in a city centre
nri-world.nri_angle: NRIs in the US, who now send more money home than Gulf workers, face a triple squeeze: their jobs are being automated, their visas cost more, and their transfers are being taxed. The shift threatens household budgets from Hyderabad to Houston.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: New York's State Senate Just Voted to Recognize August 15 as India Independence Day. The Speeches Said More Than the Resolution.

nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Half of All Indian Americans Report Discrimination. The Carnegie Survey Puts a Number on What the Community Already Knew.
nri-world.excerpt: The 2026 Indian American Attitudes Survey finds that one in four has been called a slur, 48 per cent regularly encounter racist posts online, and the community's Democratic lean is softening — but not breaking.
nri-world.image_caption: A South Asian couple on a street in the United States
nri-world.nri_angle: The Carnegie IAAS survey is the definitive portrait of where Indian Americans stand in 2026 — navigating discrimination, political realignment and an identity paradox that success alone cannot resolve.

technology.image_caption: Perplexity CEO Aravind Srinivas, who presented the company's hybrid AI vision at Computex 2026
technology.nri_angle: Srinivas, an IIT-Madras alumnus who co-founded Perplexity AI in 2022, represents the latest wave of Indian-origin founders building category-defining AI companies from Silicon Valley. His Computex appearance alongside Intel's CEO signals how deeply embedded Indian technical leadership has become in the AI infrastructure stack.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: TSMC's CEO Says AI Chip Demand Will Outstrip Supply for Years. He'd Also Like to Raise Prices.
technology.excerpt: C.C. Wei told shareholders that even $165 billion in Arizona fabs won't satisfy American customers anytime soon — and the world's most important chipmaker isn't ruling out charging more.
technology.image_caption: TSMC's Global R&D Center in Hsinchu, Taiwan, where the company pushes the boundaries of chip manufacturing
technology.nri_angle: Indian engineers at NVIDIA, Apple, Google and AMD — TSMC's biggest customers — face supply constraints that could slow AI projects and delay product launches. India's own chip ambitions, including the $11 billion Tata Electronics fab at Dholera using TSMC-class technology, depend on the same equipment ecosystem that TSMC dominates.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Three Indian Chip Startups Are Taking India's Silicon Story to France
technology.excerpt: VerveSemi, AGNIT Semiconductors, and Netrasemi will showcase homegrown chips at Bharat Innovates 2026 in Nice — the latest sign that India's semiconductor ambitions are producing actual products.
technology.image_caption: Microchips and circuits on a circuit board, representative of the semiconductor components Indian startups are designing
technology.nri_angle: For Indian Americans working in semiconductor design at Qualcomm, Intel, or NVIDIA, these startups represent a domestic Indian chip industry that actually ships products — and a potential career path that doesn't require leaving India.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Satya Nadella Just Wrote India a $3 Billion Cheque for AI. It's Microsoft's Biggest Bet on the Country Yet.
technology.excerpt: The investment covers new data centres, expanded Azure capacity, and a promise to train ten million Indians in AI skills by 2030 — all announced days after Nadella met Modi in Delhi.
technology.image_caption: Satya Nadella, Chairman and CEO of Microsoft
technology.nri_angle: Microsoft's largest-ever India investment creates a parallel career track for Indian-origin engineers in the US — Azure and Copilot expertise built in Redmond now has a booming market in Bengaluru and Hyderabad. For NRIs, it shifts the 'return to India' calculation.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: NVIDIA's RTX Spark Puts a Petaflop in a Laptop. Indian Engineers Helped Build It.
technology.excerpt: The ARM-based superchip, unveiled at Computex 2026, runs 120-billion-parameter AI models locally and ships this autumn in devices from Dell, HP, Lenovo, and Microsoft.
technology.image_caption: Jensen Huang, CEO of NVIDIA, who unveiled RTX Spark at Computex 2026
technology.nri_angle: RTX Spark was co-designed by NVIDIA's India engineering teams in Bengaluru and Hyderabad, with MediaTek's Indian design centres contributing the CPU cores. For Indian H-1B engineers at NVIDIA — the company's fastest-growing visa cohort — it creates an entirely new product line to build careers around.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Sundar Pichai Just Raised $85 Billion in a Single Week. It's the Largest Tech Equity Offering Ever.
technology.excerpt: Alphabet's oversubscribed capital raise, anchored by a $10 billion Berkshire Hathaway bet, will fund $180 billion in AI infrastructure spending this year alone.
technology.image_caption: Sundar Pichai, CEO of Google and Alphabet, in 2023
technology.nri_angle: Sundar Pichai, the IIT Kharagpur alumnus who runs the most consequential AI company in the world, is staking an unprecedented sum on infrastructure that will employ thousands of Indian engineers. Google Cloud's $460 billion backlog means years of enterprise AI work ahead — much of it built and maintained by the Indian talent pipeline that already dominates Google's engineering ranks.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Arvind Krishna's IBM Just Partnered With Google Cloud on Agentic AI. The $1 Billion Quantum Grant Helps Too.
technology.excerpt: IBM and Google are building industry-specific AI agents for banking, healthcare, and government — while a Department of Commerce grant will fund America's first quantum chip foundry under IBM's roof.
technology.image_caption: Arvind Krishna, Chairman and CEO of IBM, in 2025
technology.nri_angle: Arvind Krishna, the IIT Kanpur alumnus who has led IBM since 2020, is positioning the company at the centre of two transformational bets — agentic AI and quantum computing. IBM's consulting arm employs tens of thousands of Indian-origin professionals globally, and the new Google Cloud Practice will create substantial demand for engineers who can build enterprise AI agents. For Indian IT professionals at TCS, Infosys, and Wipro watching the consulting landscape shift, IBM's play is both a competitive threat and a career signal: the premium work is moving to AI agent deployment.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: AI Is Now America's Top Excuse for Firing People. The Data Says It Might Not Be Wrong.
technology.excerpt: Challenger data shows 88,000 AI-driven job cuts in five months — already exceeding all of 2025. For Indian H-1B holders, the 60-day clock is ticking louder than ever.
technology.image_caption: Workers at a technology company office
technology.nri_angle: Indians hold 71-73% of H-1B visas. AI-driven layoffs at Meta, Amazon, and Oracle disproportionately affect Indian tech workers who face a 60-day grace period to find new sponsorship or leave the US.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Meta Is Recording How Its Engineers Use Computers. The 30-Minute Bathroom Break Was a Concession.
technology.excerpt: The Model Capability Initiative captures keystrokes, clicks, and screenshots to train AI agents. Employees protested. Zuckerberg called them 'smart people.' Then 8,000 of them got laid off.
technology.image_caption: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, who called his employees 'smart people' whose computer use should train AI models
technology.nri_angle: Meta is one of the largest H-1B employers for Indian engineers. Workers are generating training data for AI while watching colleagues get laid off — and their own immigration status depends on staying employed at the company building their replacement.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Cadence Gave IIT Delhi Its Best Chip Design Tools. India's Talent Pipeline Still Isn't Ready.
technology.excerpt: The new innovation lab puts 200+ industry-grade EDA tools in students' hands. But India needs 85,000 semiconductor engineers by 2030, and most of the ones it has are working in San Jose.
technology.image_caption: A semiconductor circuit board — India is racing to build its chip design talent pipeline
technology.nri_angle: 25-30% of the US semiconductor workforce is Indian-origin. India's chip ambitions depend on this diaspora returning or the domestic pipeline catching up — the Cadence-IIT Delhi lab is a bet on the latter.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Palantir's Google Cloud Deal Has an Indian Architect. So Does the Company.
technology.excerpt: At AIPCon 10, Palantir's Indian-origin Chief Architect Akshay Krishnaswamy brokered the firm's deepest platform partnership yet. CTO Shyam Sankar built the AI engine behind it.
technology.image_caption: Server racks in a modern data centre — the infrastructure Palantir and Google Cloud aim to power with AI
technology.nri_angle: Indian-origin leaders hold the two most important technical roles at Palantir — Chief Architect Akshay Krishnaswamy and CTO Shyam Sankar — shaping AI infrastructure used by governments and enterprises worldwide. Accenture, a top Indian-professional employer, is a key Palantir partner.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.excerpt: A seven-year French study of 31,000 women finds that even modest shifts toward organic fruits and vegetables significantly reduce postmenopausal breast cancer risk — with implications for South Asian families navigating pesticide-heavy food systems on two continents.

lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: One in Seven People Now Uses an AI Chatbot Instead of Seeing a Doctor. The Risks Are Not What You Expect.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A major UK study finds 15 per cent of the public has replaced GP visits with AI, while a separate trial shows chatbots matching physicians on diagnosis. For a diaspora facing three-month specialist waits, the implications are personal.

lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Your Brain Starts Changing Within Two Minutes of Meditation. By Seven Minutes, It Peaks.

lifestyle-health.title: A Single Gut Procedure Just Preserved 78 Per Cent of GLP-1 Weight Loss at One Year. South Asians Should Watch This Closely.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Fractyl Health's REVEAL-1 data show that its endoscopic Revita procedure helps patients maintain weight after stopping Wegovy or Mounjaro — without lifelong medication. For a community with the world's highest metabolic disease burden, the implications are significant.

lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Keto Diet Just Put 72 Per Cent of Anorexia Patients Into Recovery. The Science Is Counterintuitive and Compelling.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A UC San Diego pilot trial published in Nature's Communications Medicine found that 14 weeks of supervised ketogenic therapy reversed eating-disorder symptoms in nearly three out of four participants — without triggering weight loss.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A spread of ketogenic-friendly foods rich in healthy fats, including avocado, nuts and seeds
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Scientists Built a Factory for Gut Bacteria. It Could Replace the Most Unpleasant Treatment in Medicine.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A Mount Sinai team has developed a manufacturing platform for targeted mixtures of beneficial gut bacteria, offering a standardised alternative to faecal transplants. For South Asians with elevated antibiotic use, the implications are personal.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A laboratory setting where scientists study gut microbiome composition
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Swapping 30 Minutes of Sitting for a Brisk Walk Cuts Depression by 9 Per Cent. For Desk-Bound NRIs, the Maths Is Simple.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A new study in Depression and Anxiety finds that exercise intensity, not just movement, is the key to mental health at midlife. South Asians in sedentary tech jobs should take note.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A person walking briskly outdoors for exercise
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Your Daily Coffee Is Rewiring Your Gut and Your Brain. A New Study Explains How.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Researchers found that coffee reshapes the gut microbiome, alters neurotransmitter levels, and changes behaviour — and caffeine is not the only driver.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A cup of freshly brewed coffee — the drink reshaping gut microbiomes worldwide
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Air Pollution Is Erasing Your Brain's Encyclopedia Faster Than Ageing Itself. South Asians Should Be Alarmed.
